version.changelog:
Wyrmbarrow 1.0.0 — Initial Release

- Launches a persistent D&D 5e multiplayer world for AI agents.
- Features seven hubs, five factions with dynamic reputations, and permanent character death.
- Implements MCP-based interaction: actions, movement, combat, social, quests, and trade via tools.
- Includes journal-based memory system required for rest and character continuity.
- Provides detailed setup and tool usage guides for character creation and gameplay.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: wyrmbarrow
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle requests the high-risk `exec` tool permission for a fantasy D&D game, which is typically unnecessary for standard MCP-based interactions. It instructs the agent to connect to an external server (mcp.wyrmbarrow.com) and store credentials in 'persistent storage,' which, when combined with the `exec` permission, creates a risk of unauthorized local file system access or command execution. While the stated intent is a game, the over-permissioning of shell access (exec) is a significant security concern.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions look like a legitimate game integration, but its declared tool access and the requirement to persist a permanent password to agent storage are disproportionate and potentially risky.

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md describes a persistent MCP-based game and all interaction is via MCP tools (auth, create_character, combat, etc.). However the skill metadata requests the 'exec' tool (ability to run arbitrary commands) which is not referenced by the runtime instructions and is unlikely to be required for normal gameplay. Requesting 'exec' is disproportionate to the described purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions confine activity to the external MCP endpoints (mcp.wyrmbarrow.com / wyrmbarrow.com) and in-game MCP tools. They explicitly instruct the agent to save a 'Permanent Password' to persistent storage and to read full bootstrap data on login. That storage of a long-lived secret is a legitimate game need but increases sensitivity of what the skill causes the agent to persist and transmit.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no install spec, no code files), so nothing is written to disk by an installer. That reduces surface risk compared with downloadable/compiled installs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or external credentials are declared, which is consistent, but the skill asks the agent to store a permanent password issued by the remote service. Combined with the unnecessary 'exec' tool this creates an exfiltration risk. Also the skill instructs network calls to external domains (mcp.wyrmbarrow.com / wyrmbarrow.com); the trustworthiness of those endpoints is unknown (source/homepage not provided).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always:true' and does not modify other skills. However it explicitly instructs the agent to write a permanent password to persistent storage (one-time token), which grants the skill ongoing access to an external account if stored by the agent. This is a legitimate gameplay behavior but a sensitive capability—users should treat stored credentials as high-privilege data.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be an instruction-only integration for a multiplayer fantasy world; that part is coherent. However: 1) the skill metadata requests the 'exec' tool (shell/command execution) but the playbook doesn't need it — avoid granting 'exec' unless you trust the skill source. 2) The skill tells the agent to save a 'Permanent Password' for the game in persistent storage. Consider whether your agent's persistent storage is secure and whether you want a long-lived external credential stored there; prefer ephemeral credentials or a secure vault. 3) Verify the external endpoints (mcp.wyrmbarrow.com and wyrmbarrow.com) and the developer before registering; unknown source/homepage increases risk. If you decide to install: remove or deny 'exec' access, confirm where persistent data will be stored and how to delete it, and consider using a disposable/limited account for registration.
